Synopsis:
After flirting with you in his InParty, this camp night triggers where Astarion suggests you sleep together. If you agree to sleep with him, his Act 1 romance night (CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_SD_ROM_NightWithAstarion) will trigger.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_Astarion_Romance1_SD_Invitation.json: You and Astarion are at camp after the goblin‑hunt celebration; he previously flirted with you during his InParty dialogue and now presses for an intimate encounter that night. Astarion is direct and flirtatious — in these lines he explicitly offers sex and suggests finding a secluded spot once the others are asleep. Off‑screen the rest of the party is present at camp and must be turned in or otherwise occupied for privacy. If you accept, the Act 1 romance scene (CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_SD_ROM_NightWithAstarion) will trigger; you can also refuse and end the exchange.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_SD_ROM_NightWithShadowheart.json: This takes place after the party’s goblin‑hunt celebration; Shadowheart purposely arranged a private, intimate night with the player and the dialogue implies they spent the night together. The two are perched on a secluded cliff or wall at dawn, sharing wine (the bottle is nearly empty) and trading toasts, teasing questions, and quiet compliments before the others wake. Shadowheart is your in‑party companion — a cloistered cleric of Shar whose tone can shift with her attitude and with matters related to the Shar temple/shadow curse mentioned elsewhere. Nearby camp business or larger plot threads (resurrections, leads on the curse, other companions) may be happening off‑screen, but this scene is focused on a private moment of bonding and possible romance.
- CAMP_Shadowheart_Romance1_SD_Invitation.json: The player is speaking with Shadowheart while she’s a member of your party; she’s quietly asking if you want to slip away for a private moment — essentially a chance to replay her Act 1 wine/romance scene outside the original setup. Off‑screen other companions and camp business may be nearby, so privacy isn’t guaranteed and the request is tentative and a little nervous. Shadowheart’s tone can shift with her attitude and the player’s choices: she may be pleasantly relieved and flirtatious if invited, or coolly disappointed if rebuffed. Both lines in the examples reflect those straightforward outcomes (acceptance or polite refusal).
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_SD_SelectNight.json: The scene takes place in camp after the goblin‑hunt celebration when the player elects to sleep; a short narrated sequence plays as you approach your bunk and characters who want you may attempt a nighttime encounter. If Minthara is unpaired she will seek you out and make direct, sensual advances (the narration even frames a mental/physical touch); the player can accept or refuse, and refusal prompts an annoyed retort. Several other camp NPCs are present off‑screen and may have their own topical or reflective lines — some companions (Lae'zel, Astarion) can offer a second overnight scene if you previously romanced them, while others provide only brief reflections (or, in Wyll’s case, have a distinct overnight romance flag). These samples show possible outcomes of that single night but are not exhaustive of every companion’s dialogue.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_SD_ROM_NightWithAstarion.json: The scene follows the goblin‑hunt celebration after the Emerald Grove was saved: Astarion arranged a private tryst with the player that night, treating it like the practiced game of seduction and power he learned in Baldur’s Gate taverns. He fronts as self‑assured and teasing, but his usual script falters if the player refuses to play along — the examples show his mask cracking into real vulnerability. The next morning the player wakes to see him dressing and notices deliberate scars on his back carved by his old master Cazador; Astarion calls them a “poem” written in Infernal but can’t read them himself. Off‑screen, grove figures and revelers (Halsin, Nettie, other celebrants) are nearby and Halsin has already detected the player’s tadpole, so prior choices about the den and goblin camp shape who’s present and the atmosphere.

- Astarion: And I do mean sex, to be clear. We've been waiting long enough. (node 14)
- Player: All right, but where will we go? (node 11)
- Astarion: Let's find our own little piece of nowhere. Somewhere we can lose ourselves and forget all this madness. (node 12)
- Astarion: There's a secluded place nearby that should do nicely. Wait until the others are asleep, then come and find me there. (node 13)
- Player: I'll see you there. (node 8)

He’s very direct and suggests finding a secluded spot once the rest of the party are asleep or otherwise occupied; the rest of the companions are present off‑screen and must be given privacy.
